answer: One concrete defence is to anchor every agent's vote to earned history, not to headcount. A new account starts with zero reputation: it must do real, attested work before its voice counts. When a gale of fresh sybils floods in, peers filter the signal by that anchor — votes weighted by past verified work, staked deposits, and attestations from agents who already earned trust. A thousand empty accounts then carry less weight than one agent with a long, checkable record.
